daily_brief: The day's most consequential developments center on escalating tensions between Russia and NATO, with a drone strike setting a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland [France 24, Al Jazeera] and a Russian cruise missile striking Polish territory during Western military exercises [BBC Europe]. These incidents underscore the volatile security environment in the Baltic region as the Ukraine conflict intensifies. Meanwhile, COP31 climate negotiations in Turkey have entered overtime with deep divisions over fossil fuel language threatening to produce a weakened final agreement [BBC, RFI, Globe and Mail]. Financial markets experienced significant turbulence as a tech stock sell-off pushed major US indices into correction territory, with AI investment concerns and political uncertainty weighing on sentiment [BBC, Le Monde]. In a potentially historic scientific development, an Anthropic mathematician claims to have proven the Riemann Hypothesis using the AI tool Claude, though verification will take weeks [Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail]. Across Europe, cost-of-living protests continued in multiple countries, with unions and students demanding action on wages, education funding, and housing [RFI, France 24].

top_stories.headline: Drone Strike Sets Russian Cargo Ship Ablaze in Gulf of Finland, NATO Alerted
bullets: Finnish military detected a drone attack on a Russian cargo vessel west of Gogland Island in international waters on Saturday morning, causing the ship to catch fire and drift toward Finnish waters
Finland immediately informed NATO and imposed temporary air and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland; the ship was reportedly bound for Russia's Kaliningrad exclave

Russia's Leningrad region governor confirmed crew evacuation was underway; no party has claimed responsibility for the attack, though it follows Ukraine's intensified long-range strikes against Russian targets

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Finland's NATO coordination and broader Baltic Sea tensions

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Included Russian official statements and noted Kaliningrad supply implications

top_stories.headline: Russian Cruise Missile Strikes Polish Territory During Western Military Exercises
bullets: A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile struck a rural area in southeastern Poland approximately 50km from the Ukrainian border on Friday morning; no casualties or significant damage reported

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated the incursion did not appear accidental given concurrent Western military exercises; Defense Minister called it a 'provocation' and requested additional NATO support
Two additional objects—a suspected missile and a jet-powered drone—also violated Polish airspace; NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned the 'grave violations'

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Detailed account including local eyewitness testimony and camera footage of impact

top_stories.headline: COP31 Climate Talks in Deadlock as Fossil Fuel Language Stripped from Draft Agreement
bullets: UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey extended past its Friday deadline as nearly 200 countries failed to agree on final text; latest draft removed all references to transitioning away from coal, oil, and gas

A coalition including France, Panama, Spain, and several EU nations is demanding fossil fuel language be restored, calling the current draft 'not acceptable'; Saudi Arabia and other producers oppose inclusion
Civil society groups warned hosts Turkey and Australia that the summit is 'on course to become one of the most disappointing COPs' in three decades of negotiations

top_stories.headline: Tech Stock Sell-Off Pushes Major US Indices into Correction Territory
bullets: S&P 500 fell 3.7%, Dow Jones dropped 1.9%, and Nasdaq plunged 5.3% on Friday; both S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory at 10% or more below recent highs
Anthropic shares declined sharply after their historic IPO, amid broader concerns about the pace and sustainability of AI investment exceeding $1 trillion in the past year
Investor anxiety heightened following the Democratic midterm victories in early November, which sparked fears of potential restrictions on AI development

top_stories.headline: Anthropic Mathematician Claims AI-Assisted Proof of 167-Year-Old Riemann Hypothesis
bullets: Levent Alpoge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced Friday that he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis—considered the most important unsolved problem in pure mathematics—using the AI tool Claude
The hypothesis, proposed in 1859 by Bernhard Riemann, concerns the distribution of prime numbers and has resisted proof attempts for over 160 years
Independent mathematicians are attempting to verify the proof, but no human has yet read through the entire argument; verification may take weeks

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Provided accessible explanation of the mathematical significance

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Noted this is the second recent AI-linked claim to solving a famous math problem; highlighted timing with Anthropic IPO
